correctness.rationale: Auel--Singer's defining equations make coordinate squaring a finite map to the projective plane of magic squares. A generic squared magic square has exactly 2^9/2=256 projective square-root lifts, equal to the order of the sign subgroup S, so the function-field extension is Galois with group S. Standard transitivity of a Galois group on valuations above a fixed prime divisor makes each 64-component diagonal preimage one S-orbit. The explicit reflection exchanges the two quotient lines, so all 128 conics form one G-orbit; orbit--stabilizer gives orders 4 and 16. The finite pattern and order calculations are replayed by verify_orbit.py.

value.rationale: The source explicitly leaves classification of all conics open. Collapsing the complete known 128-conic catalogue to one automorphism orbit is a natural structural lemma for that problem: one representative controls every known conic, any additional conic must lie in another orbit, and the stabilizer orders provide quantitative symmetry data for subsequent orbit/incidence calculations. This is not a mere renaming or recomputation of the component count.
